title: Routing Audit Entry
description: One immutable entry in the routing audit log. Entries are appended, never amended: a decision and what it later turned out to cost are two events, because the second is not known when the first is made. `selected` records which Deployment a connection target was set to and on what grounds; `attributed` records who the ledger says actually paid for the requests that followed.

id.description: Content hash of the entry, computed like an Evidence id over the entry with `id` removed.

grounds.description: Why this Deployment and not another. `explicit` means the operator named it, `recommendation` means a ranking chose it, `existing` means the profile already pointed at it, `interactive` means it was picked from a list. Recording the outcome without this cannot answer why, which is what an auditable route has to answer.

recommendationId.description: The Recommendation this selection came from, when grounds is `recommendation`. Its own record carries the rule, the profile version and the evidence behind the ranking, so the audit cites it rather than copying it.

selectionId.description: The `selected` entry this attribution belongs to.

attribution.description: What the billing ledger reported for the requests that followed the selection. Absent requests are not an absence of cost: settlement lags, and `unconfirmed` says so rather than claiming either outcome.
